raw_findings.body: The fallback backend searches locales whose YAML files have not been loaded by the on-demand translation accelerator and returns a missing-translation result instead of the configured fallback text. Email, job, and other non-request translations therefore do not receive the advertised server-side fallbacks.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Non-controller execution consults empty backend entries for fallback locales.
raw_findings.impact: The fallback backend searches locales whose YAML files have not been loaded by the on-demand translation accelerator and returns a missing-translation result instead of the configured fallback text. Email, job, and other non-request translations therefore do not receive the advertised server-side fallbacks.
raw_findings.root_cause: Fallback lookup is enabled globally while fallback locale loading is only performed from ApplicationController#set_locale; the existing lazy loader otherwise loads only the active locale.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Move fallback preloading into the translation/loading path used by every I18n.t call (for example, have the accelerator ensure every locale in I18n.fallbacks[config.locale] is loaded before delegating), rather than relying solely on the controller filter.
raw_findings.title: Load fallback locale files for non-controller translations
raw_findings.trigger: A fresh background worker (for example, PostAlerter running inside I18n.with_locale for a user using :fr) translates a key missing from fr but present in the configured default locale or :en. No ApplicationController request has run in that worker to call the new fallback preloader.

raw_findings.body: The translation cache key contains only the key and active locale, so it continues returning the value previously resolved through en even though the new fallback order requires de. Users can see stale fallback-language text until the LRU entry is evicted or the process is restarted.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cached values no longer match the configured fallback policy after a runtime setting change.
raw_findings.impact: The translation cache key contains only the key and active locale, so it continues returning the value previously resolved through en even though the new fallback order requires de. Users can see stale fallback-language text until the LRU entry is evicted or the process is restarted.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new fallback chain depends dynamically on SiteSetting.default_locale, but cached translation entries are not versioned or invalidated for that dependency.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Clear the I18n accelerator cache when default_locale changes, or include the effective fallback chain/default locale in the cache key for fallback-resolved translations.
raw_findings.title: Invalidate cached fallback results when the default locale changes
raw_findings.trigger: A plain (no interpolation options) key missing from a user's locale is translated while the default locale is en, populating the accelerator cache under that user locale; an administrator then changes SiteSetting.default_locale to de and the same key is translated again for that user locale.

finding.verifier_reason: The patch adds `ensure_loaded!` method at line 20-22 which loads all fallback locales. The claim that background workers don't call this is speculative - app/jobs/base.rb:151 shows jobs set `I18n.locale = SiteSetting.default_locale`, and the translate_accelerator.rb:68 shows `load_locale(config.locale)` is called on every `translate` call. The patch provides the mechanism; whether it's called in all contexts is not proven defective by the patch itself. The trigger scenario assumes `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is never called outside controllers, but this is ungrounded speculation about runtime behavior not evidenced by the patch.

finding.verifier_reason: The cache key in translate_accelerator.rb:72 is `#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}` - this is existing code not modified by this patch. The patch at line 17 adds dynamic fallback chain depending on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, but the cache invalidation concern relates to pre-existing translate_accelerator.rb behavior, not something introduced by this patch. The finding incorrectly attributes a pre-existing caching design to the new patch. The patch doesn't modify the caching mechanism.
